Why no honest @estop exists: the whole upstream class XYZMotion:VXM (XYZMotion.py:27-220, 194 lines) defines exactly __init__, home, sendcmd, getresp, waitReady, getPosition, getAllPositions, setVelocity, moveToZero, move_mm, move_in and __del__ (which closes the port). There is no stop, abort, halt, disable or free-run method. waitReady sends 'V' and only waits until the reply is 'R'; the comment says B is busy, R is ready, J is jog/slew mode and b is jogging (XYZMotion.py:66-79), so the query does not cancel a move. moveToZero and move_mm/move_in start motion (lines 171-215); home() runs three of those moves (lines 37-44); __del__ closes the serial port (lines 219-220) and cannot stop the controller. A move already started therefore cannot be cancelled through this library. DRV-012 requires @estop to reach the real native stop, so any @estop here would be a no-op or would invent a VXM stop command that the clone does not contain; invented wire syntax and invented facts are excluded, so the package is blocked instead of faked. This is the same conclusion as the blocked package quantumquadrate__k10cr1.

The clone also cannot be imported safely. The module executes XYZ = VXM(port, baud, maxWaitTime) at line 224, then XYZ.home(), XYZ.move_in('X',1), XYZ.move_in('Y',2), XYZ.move_in('Z',2.5) and another XYZ.home() (lines 224-236). Any 'from XYZMotion import VXM' opens COM4 and moves the stage. This package therefore ships no native.py and no hardware backend; driver.lock.json backends is {"fake": ".fake:FakeVxm"}. The gate never imports the clone, and no hardware was attached.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card proposes a SerialDriver (family serial, decision family-config), but every command is assembled from a prefix and a run-time number ('E,C,S1M' + str(Speed) + ',R' and the I1M/I2M/I3M forms, XYZMotion.py:156-167, 171-195, 201-215), so a command table cannot reproduce the wire lines and G7 would not find them. This package is a direct Driver over XYZMotion:VXM with a fake backend.

Coverage (fake only): position read in mm from getPosition (0.0050 mm/step, line 20); velocity_x/y/z writes in steps/s bounded by the clone's 1-6000 range (line 155), with the last commanded value readable (the clone has no velocity query, so this is not a read-back); cap.motion.home.v1 with an optional axes subset (native home() for all, moveToZero for a subset); cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 for an absolute X/Y/Z move in mm, implemented as read-current + relative move_mm per axis. The clone states no axis travel, so the three position inputs are Limit.operator_required and site-limits.example.json shows an example envelope. No extension ids are used. The fake is an in-memory stand-in, not a transcript: the clone has no simulator, tests or recording; every number in fake.py is marked '# placeholder'. NOT COVERED: move_in (the inch wrapper of the same command), getAllPositions' English-unit path (its Y divides by 24.4 while getPosition divides by 25.4, line 140), the raw serial transport, and the module-level convenience script.
